extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies, Native American Tribes, state and local governments, industry, organizations, and members of the public invited to review and comment on the Draft LANL Site-Wide EIS
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive instructions for submitting and participating in public comment on the Draft Site-Wide Environmental Impact Statement (SWEIS) for continued operation of Los Alamos National Laboratory, including hearing formats, submission channels, privacy notices, and the alternatives analyzed in the Draft SWEIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period / deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: NNSA invites review and submission of comments on the Draft LANL SWEIS through March 11, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NNSA will consider all comments received or postmarked by the end of the comment period in preparing the Final LANL SWEIS. Comments received or postmarked after the comment period will be considered to the extent practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments on the Draft LANL SWEIS should be emailed to LANLSWEIS@nnsa.doe.gov or mailed to Mr. Stephen Hoffman, LANL SWEIS Document Manager, DOE/NNSA, 3747 W. Jemez Road, Los Alamos, New Mexico 87544.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Draft LANL SWEIS is available online at https://www.energy.gov/nnsa/nnsa-nepa-reading-room and https://www.energy.gov/nepa/listings/latest-documents-and-notices. Copies also available for review at the LANL Public Reading Room at 94 Cities of Gold Road, Pojoaque, New Mexico.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of written and verbal comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Written and verbal comments will be given equal weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments provided at public hearings (verbal) are considered equivalent to written comments for purposes of agency consideration; formal public comments at hearings will be transcribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voicemail and accepted comment formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on the Draft SWEIS will not be accepted via the voicemail system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only written comments or those provided at a public hearing will be accepted. A phone voicemail may be used to leave a message for information but is not an accepted method for submitting comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing format and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For in-person hearings NNSA will hold an Open House for the first 30 minutes, then a presentation on the Draft SWEIS (~30 minutes), followed by clarifying questions about the comment process, and then formal public comments with transcription by a court stenographer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NNSA will not answer questions during the formal public comment period. The two Feb 11 hearings offer a virtual option for the presentation and public comment portions. Times, dates, and locations are listed in the notice; any changes will be published and noticed at least 15 days before hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual participation and advance notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Two public hearings will include a virtual component for remote participation in the presentation and public comment portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virtual hearing access instructions (e.g., website link or phone number) will be announced at least 15 days before the hearing and will be published in local newspapers, noticed to the GovDelivery mailing list, and available on DOE/NNSA websites listed in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability, redaction, and posting of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means comments posted on Regulations.gov or agency sites may be redacted or withheld at agency discretion and may not appear immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personally identifiable information (PII), anonymity, and requests to withhold
rubrics_metrics.description: Before including your address, phone number, email address, or other personally identifiable information in your comment, be advised that your entire comment—including your personally identifiable information—may be made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish for NNSA to withhold your name and/or other personally identifiable information, state this prominently at the beginning of your comment. You may submit comments anonymously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives analyzed — No-Action Alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: The No-Action Alternative: NNSA would continue current facility operations throughout LANL in support of assigned missions. Includes previously completed NEPA-reviewed activities, construction of new facilities, modernization and upgrade projects, DD&D of excess/aging facilities, legacy cleanup and remediation per the Consent Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The No-Action Alternative includes 87 new projects totaling almost 1.5 million square feet (2024–2038), 11 projects affecting about 216 acres, and about 1.6 million square feet of DD&D; examples include increased plutonium pit production and remediation of a chromium plume in Mortandad Canyon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives analyzed — Modernized Operations Alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: The Modernized Operations Alternative: includes the scope of the No-Action Alternative plus additional modernization activities—construction of replacement facilities, upgrades to facilities/utilities/infrastructure, and DD&D to extend facility life and improve work environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernized Operations includes proposed projects to reduce greenhouse gases and emissions; 139 new projects totaling over 3.4 million square feet (2025–2038); 27 projects affecting about 925 acres (up to 795 acres proposed for up to 159 megawatts of solar PV arrays); and an additional 1.2 million square feet of DD&D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives analyzed — Expanded Operations Alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: The Expanded Operations Alternative: includes the Modernized Operations actions plus actions that would expand operations and missions to meet increasing requirements, including construction/operation of new facilities to expand capabilities beyond current ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanded Operations includes 18 additional new projects (about 947,000 square feet) to be implemented between 2025–2038, and 4 additional utilities/infrastructure projects affecting about 46 acres; examples include revised wildland fire risk reduction treatments and management of feral cattle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-comment process and Record of Decision timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the public comment period, and after consideration of comments received, NNSA will prepare the Final LANL SWEIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about future operations at the Laboratory will be provided in an NNSA Record of Decision published in the Federal Register, which would be issued no sooner than 30 days after publication by the Environmental Protection Agency of the notice of availability of the Final LANL SWEIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and update distribution for hearing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes or updates to the public hearings will be published in local newspapers, posted on DOE and NNSA websites, and distributed through notices to the GovDelivery mailing list at least 15 days before the hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the channels and minimum advance notice (15 days) for changes to hearing logistics or virtual access information.
